title: Inside an agent run: a tool call, a retry and an answer
objectives: Follow the message flow of one Pydantic AI run, node by node.
Explain what ModelRetry does when a tool rejects its arguments.

steps.title: The learner's question
steps.payload_excerpt: Do I need an umbrella in SF today?

annotation.why: Every run starts from one prompt. Run state lives in the message history.

steps.title: Instructions travel with the prompt
steps.summary: Instructions are sent on every request but are not saved in history.
steps.payload_excerpt: You are a weather assistant. Use get_forecast; never guess the weather.

annotation.why: `instructions=` is re-sent each request, so it always reflects the agent's current code.

steps.title: Request 1 to the model
steps.summary: The agent sends the message history and the tool list to the model.

annotation.why: One graph node per model call. A run is a loop of request, then tool calls, then request.

checkpoint.prompt: The model has the question and one tool, get_forecast. What does the agent do next?
checkpoint.explanation: The instructions say never to guess, so the model returns a get_forecast tool call.

steps.title: The model calls get_forecast
steps.summary: The model returns a tool call instead of text.

annotation.why: The model cannot run code. It names a tool and arguments; the agent runs it.

checkpoint.prompt: The model called get_forecast with city='SF', which the tool rejects with ModelRetry. What happens?
options: The error goes to the user
The message goes back to the model for another try
checkpoint.explanation: ModelRetry becomes a retry prompt in the history, and the model gets another request.

steps.title: The tool asked the model to try again
steps.summary: get_forecast raised ModelRetry; the message goes back to the model.
steps.payload_excerpt:
City not found, try the full name

Fix the errors and try again.

annotation.why: Raising ModelRetry turns a tool failure into feedback the model can act on; no crash.

steps.title: Request 2 to the model
steps.summary: The agent sends the message history and the tool list to the model.

annotation.why: One graph node per model call. A run is a loop of request, then tool calls, then request.

steps.title: The model calls get_forecast
steps.summary: The model returns a tool call instead of text.

annotation.why: The model cannot run code. It names a tool and arguments; the agent runs it.
The tool return value is added to history as a ToolReturnPart.

steps.title: Request 3 to the model
steps.summary: The agent sends the message history and the tool list to the model.

annotation.why: One graph node per model call. A run is a loop of request, then tool calls, then request.

steps.title: The model answers
steps.payload_excerpt: Rain, 14 C. Yes, bring an umbrella to San Francisco today.

annotation.why: A text answer with no tool call ends the run. FunctionModel scripted all of this, so no API key was needed.

takeaways: A run is a loop: model request, tool calls, model request, until the model returns text.
ModelRetry feeds a tool error back to the model instead of failing the run.
FunctionModel lets you script the model, so tests and traces need no API key.
